description: Overall health of this node: how current its ledgers are, how much time it spends fully synced, I/O and job-queue responsiveness, ledger-fetch and history-integrity signals, and job execution and wait timings.

panels.title: Validated Ledger Age [$xrpl_network_type]
panels.description:
**What:** Seconds since the most recently validated ledger, i.e. how far behind the network the node is.
**How it's computed:** Current value of the validated-ledger-age gauge per node.
**Reading it:** Lower is better; a healthy node stays within a few ledger-close intervals.
**Healthy range:** under ~10s (the network closes a ledger every 3-5s).
**Watch for:** Above 20s or climbing steadily (the node is falling behind or has lost sync).
**Source:** src/xrpld/app/ledger/LedgerMaster.h LedgerMaster::Stats ctor

targets.expr: ledgermaster_validated_ledger_age{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name"}

panels.title: Published Ledger Age [$xrpl_network_type]
panels.description:
**What:** Seconds since the most recently published ledger (the ledger exposed to clients and subscribers).
**How it's computed:** Current value of the published-ledger-age gauge per node.
**Reading it:** Should track validated-ledger age closely.
**Healthy range:** under ~10s.
**Watch for:** Published age growing while validated age stays low (publish-pipeline backlog).
**Source:** src/xrpld/app/ledger/LedgerMaster.h LedgerMaster::Stats ctor

targets.expr: ledgermaster_published_ledger_age{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name"}

panels.title: Ledger Fetch Rate [$xrpl_network_type]
panels.description:
**What:** Rate at which the node requests ledgers from peers.
**How it's computed:** Per-second rate of the ledger-fetches counter over 5 minutes.
**Reading it:** Near zero when synced; rises when catching up or backfilling history.
**Healthy range:** workload-dependent; low on a synced node.
**Watch for:** Sustained high fetch rate on a node that should be current (repeatedly missing ledgers).
**Source:** src/xrpld/app/ledger/detail/InboundLedgers.cpp InboundLedgersImp ctor

targets.expr: rate(ledger_fetches_total{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name"}[$__rate_interval])

panels.title: Ledger History Mismatches [$xrpl_network_type]
panels.description:
**What:** Rate of ledger-history hash mismatches: built ledgers whose hash disagrees with the validated hash.
**How it's computed:** Per-second rate of the history-mismatch counter over 5 minutes.
**Reading it:** Should be flat at zero.
**Healthy range:** zero.
**Watch for:** Any non-zero value (consensus divergence, corrupted history, or database issues).
**Source:** src/xrpld/telemetry/MetricsRegistry.cpp incrementLedgerHistoryMismatch (caller LedgerHistory.cpp)

targets.expr: rate(ledger_history_mismatch_total{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name"}[$__rate_interval])

panels.title: Operating Mode (Time Share)
panels.description:
**What:** Fraction of time in each operating mode (per-interval): Disconnected, Connected, Syncing, Tracking, Full.
**How it's computed:** Per-mode duration rate divided by the sum of all five mode rates over the interval; the five shares stack to 100%.
**Reading it:** Full should fill almost the entire band on a healthy node.
**Healthy range:** Full near 100%; other modes near 0.
**Watch for:** A rising share of Syncing, Connected, or Disconnected (instability or repeated resync).
**Source:** src/xrpld/app/misc/NetworkOPs.cpp NetworkOPsImp::Stats ctor

panels.title: Operating Mode Transitions
panels.description:
**What:** Transitions into each operating mode, per interval.
**How it's computed:** round(increase(...[$__interval])) over the per-mode transition counters. $__interval tiles the buckets exactly, so each bar is the transitions in that bucket and the legend Total is the true count; $__rate_interval would overlap each bucket by one scrape and inflate it (measured +5% at a 36h range, +26% zoomed in). round() removes increase()'s extrapolation, which otherwise reports fractional counts. The series stays correct across an xrpld restart (the counters reset to 0).
**Reading it:** Few transitions is good; a stable node rarely leaves Full. Brief flaps are visible here even when they are too short to appear on Operating Mode (State Timeline), which can only sample state once per scrape.
**Healthy range:** workload-dependent; low and infrequent transitions.
**Watch for:** Frequent transitions out of Full, or any into Disconnected/Syncing (flapping).
**Source:** src/xrpld/app/misc/NetworkOPs.cpp NetworkOPsImp::Stats ctor

targets.expr: round(increase(state_accounting_full_transitions{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name"}[$__interval]))

panels.title: I/O Latency
panels.description:
**What:** P95 and P50 latency of the I/O service loop, i.e. how long a queued timer callback waits to run.
**How it's computed:** 95th and 50th percentiles over a 5-minute window.
**Reading it:** Low and flat is good; this reflects event-loop responsiveness.
**Healthy range:** single-digit milliseconds; over ~10ms is notable, over ~500ms is bad.
**Watch for:** Rising P95 (thread-pool saturation or blocking work on the I/O thread).
**Source:** src/xrpld/app/main/Application.cpp ApplicationImp ctor

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, service_instance_id) (rate(ios_latency_milliseconds_bucket{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name"}[5m])))

panels.title: Job Queue Depth
panels.description:
**What:** Number of jobs currently waiting in the job queue.
**How it's computed:** Current value of the job-count gauge per node.
**Reading it:** Near zero when the node keeps up; brief spikes during heavy work are normal.
**Healthy range:** low, returning to baseline quickly.
**Watch for:** Sustained high depth (node cannot process work fast enough: replay, heavy RPC, or overload).
**Source:** src/libxrpl/core/detail/JobQueue.cpp JobQueue ctor

targets.expr: job_count{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name"}

panels.title: FullBelowCache Hit Rate [$xrpl_network_type]
panels.description:
**What:** Hit-rate percentage of the FullBelowCache.
**How it's computed:** Current value of the cache hit-rate gauge (0-100%).
**Reading it:** Higher is better; means the node reuses knowledge of complete subtrees.
**Healthy range:** above ~50% in steady state.
**Watch for:** Low hit rate during steady state (cache too small or constant re-acquisition).
**Source:** include/xrpl/basics/TaggedCache.h TaggedCache::Stats ctor

targets.expr: node_family_full_below_cache_hit_rate{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name"}

panels.title: Ledger Publish Gap [$xrpl_network_type]
panels.description:
**What:** Difference between published and validated ledger ages: how far the publish pipeline trails validation.
**How it's computed:** Published-ledger age minus validated-ledger age, in seconds.
**Reading it:** Near zero means publishing keeps up with validation.
**Healthy range:** within a few seconds of zero.
**Watch for:** A growing gap (publish backlog, stale data for subscribers).
**Source:** src/xrpld/app/ledger/LedgerMaster.h LedgerMaster::Stats ctor

panels.title: Key Jobs Execution Time
panels.description:
**What:** Execution time of the most important job types (accept/advance ledger, transaction, write objects, heartbeat, sweep, trusted validation/proposal, publish, client RPC, ledger data) at the selected quantile.
**How it's computed:** Selected quantile of each job's execution-time histogram over 5 minutes.
**Reading it:** Lower and stable is better; shows where consensus, transaction, and maintenance time goes.
**Healthy range:** workload-dependent; most jobs in low tens of milliseconds.
**Watch for:** One job type spiking (a specific bottleneck) or broad increases (overload).
**Source:** include/xrpl/core/JobTypeData.h JobTypeData ctor

panels.title: Key Jobs Dequeue Wait Time
panels.description:
**What:** Time key jobs wait in the queue before they start running, at the selected quantile.
**How it's computed:** Selected quantile of each job's queue-wait histogram over 5 minutes.
**Reading it:** Low wait means the scheduler keeps up; high wait means backlog.
**Healthy range:** workload-dependent; short waits.
**Watch for:** Rising wait across job types (queue congestion delaying consensus and transaction work).
**Source:** include/xrpl/core/JobTypeData.h JobTypeData ctor

panels.title: FullBelowCache Size
panels.description:
**What:** Number of entries in the FullBelowCache, which tracks tree nodes known to have all children present locally.
**How it's computed:** Current value of the cache-size gauge per node.
**Reading it:** Grows as the node learns complete subtrees; helps avoid redundant fetches.
**Healthy range:** workload-dependent; stable once synced.
**Watch for:** Collapsing to near zero repeatedly (cache thrash) alongside rising fetch traffic.
**Source:** include/xrpl/basics/TaggedCache.h TaggedCache::Stats ctor

targets.expr: node_family_full_below_cache_size{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name"}

panels.title: State Duration Rate (Full vs Tracking)
panels.description:
**What:** How fast the node accrues time in Full versus Tracking mode, normalized to seconds per second.
**How it's computed:** Per-second rate of the Full and Tracking accumulated-time gauges, scaled to seconds.
**Reading it:** Full rate near 1.0 means the node is in Full essentially all the time.
**Healthy range:** Full rate ~1.0, Tracking near 0.
**Watch for:** Full rate dropping below 1.0 with Tracking rising (time being lost to non-Full modes).
**Source:** src/xrpld/app/misc/NetworkOPs.cpp NetworkOPsImp::Stats ctor

targets.expr: rate(state_accounting_full_duration{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name"}[$__rate_interval]) / 1000000

rate(state_accounting_tracking_duration{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name"}[$__rate_interval]) / 1000000

panels.title: All Jobs Execution Time (Detail)
panels.description:
**What:** Execution time for all non-special job types at the selected quantile.
**How it's computed:** Selected quantile of each job's execution-time histogram over 5 minutes.
